name: Faculty in Focus: Professor Iqtidar Khan

content.title: Faculty in Focus: Professor Iqtidar Khan
content.summary: Having spent nearly three decades with AKU, Professor Khan recounts his journey with the University and shares what he has planned for the next chapter of his life.

content.text: Esteemed faculty, paediatrician and Interim Chair of AKU's Division of Women and Child Health: Professor Iqtidar Khan, was recently recognised for his contributions to the University over nearly three decades, surrounded by colleagues, family and friends. The Medical College communications team sat down with him as he recounted his AKU journey and shared what he has planned for the next chapter of his life.
When you look back on your journey with the University, what would you say has been the most fulfilling experience for you?

My most fulfilling experience has been the opportunity to witness the growth of my students, interns, residents, fellows and faculty. It is both gratifying and a pleasure to see them succeed in their respective fields.
What in your opinion has been your greatest accomplishment or honour?

There are a few that stand out quite vividly in my memory. Probably my greatest accomplishment was to lead the AKU medical-relief team during the 2010-11 floods.  We set up over 50 medical centres and offered treatment to over 1.3 million distressed persons in 15 districts of Sindh, southern Punjab and Balochistan. I believe all this was only possible with the help of the Almighty, and with support from AKU and United States Agency for International Development (USAID) funding.  Another was to be able to help thousands of patients from underprivileged backgrounds-those admitted to AKUH as well as those visiting our outpatient clinics-with help from the University's patient welfare team. Besides that, I was fortunate to help build a separate paediatric emergency room and develop subspecialties. I was also given the opportunity to lead the user committee for establishing the Faculty Office Building at Stadium Road campus, Karachi. Finally, being asked to hold down the clinical and administrative fort as Interim Chair, Division of Women and Child Health, to allow for my dear colleague, Dr Zulfiqar Bhutta, the flexibility to pursue national and international commitment is definitely something I will always cherish.
Has there been a certain person or group of people that have had a positive impact on your journey with AKU?

The Founding President of AKU Shamsh Kassim-Lakha and his successor, President Firoz Rasul, as well as the Deans and CEOs over the years have always expressed full confidence in me. They have empowered me to exercise full authority to help make the necessary changes to improve our patient and student outcomes at AKU. I feel that I have also learned a lot from our two Emeritus Professors: Gaffar Billoo and Bo Lindblad. And of course, my partnership with Professor Zulfiqar Bhutta has no match. We have stood together, not only for ourselves but also for AKU and Pakistan.
With your new role as a non-full time Professor in the Division of Women and Child Health, what is the one thing (or few things) that you look forward to dedicating your time towards?

I have never seen a single patient privately as I have served mostly in teaching hospitals in Pakistan and in the UK and Canada. So to work in the private sector is something I will have to adjust to. I have full trust in the Almighty and I pray for my good health and for my family's. I will continue to work with everyone at AKU and hope to contribute as much as I can for AKU and Pakistan.

You've been a mentor and role model to so many faculty, staff, students and trainees over the last 28 years of your association with AKU. What advice or words of wisdom would you offer to our Medical College alumni?

My advice to them is to: Be patient and respect each other. Be honest and straightforward while doing your best. Leave the results to God. You will have successes: professionally, financially and personally. Do not go for shortcuts and half-baked decisions/actions. Speak out; you will be heard. Be leaders of change for the betterment of humanity.
